subject: Multi-season model with direct and indirect observations

messages.author: af5f4b11b923f07b
messages.subject: Multi-season model with direct and indirect observations
parts:
Hello everyone,

I want to model the occupancy of a eurpoean lizard (Timon lepidus) from a study of 6 years, for 79 sites. I have 3 replicates per year and different variables (site-specific and time-specific). For each journey, we have the detection or no of the species, and we have the presence or no of indices from the species (faeces, footsteps and moults).

I want to know if there is a possibility to use direct and indirect detection (indices) to model multi-season occupancy in this case. 
I searched for different possibilities but I don't find a very interedting one...

Best regards,
Goulvenn

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Multi-season model with direct and indirect observations
parts:
You probably want to look at "multistate occupancy models".  Typically "multistate" is applied to the "occupancy" part of the model such that rather than just presence or absence of lizards you might have "present and breeding", "present and not breeding", and "not present".  But in your case the multiple categories seem to be just in the detection part:  (1) observations that clearly identify occupancy, (2) observations that are just consistent with occupancy, and (3) no indication of occupancy.  If the probability of (2) is much higher in occupied sites than in unoccupied sites, the use of such lower-level detection observations can reduce the variability in the estimators of the occupancy probabilities.

Creating the model and finding the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters is not unsurmountable but it would be a whole lot easier if some software already existed.  If no software exists, then a first step might be to set up the model and estimation code for individual years.

Jim

Hi,

Thank you for your help.

Your answer confirms my research because I had also thought of this possibility. Moreover, I had seen a publication that uses multi states for multi seasons (I can't find it anymore...). If I remember correctly, the parameters between seasons estimate the change in state of observations 0 to 1, 1 to 2 and 2 to 0. These parameters are useless in my case and this model does not estimate an extinction or colonization overall, as I need.
I will keep you inform if I find it again.

I don't really understand this part of your answer:

"Creating the model and finding the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters is not unsurmountable but it would be a whole lot easier if some software already existed.  If no software exists, then a first step might be to set up the model and estimation code for individual years."

Do you think about calculating parameters like colonisation and extinction myself for multi season from model of individual years? If it is the case, I am not sure that I am capable of it. 

Goulvenn

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Multi-season model with direct and indirect observations
parts:
Sorry, I wasn't very clear with my words.  I'm about to leave for a long trip today but when I'm done with that I'll send a better response.

In short, whether or not the desired software package exists, it wouldn't hurt to run colext with just the "direct indices" to get estimates of colonization and extinction probabilities.  That analysis is not "wrong" but just maybe inefficient.  Those estimates will likely be similar to what one would obtain with both the "direct" and "indirect" indices except that if one can include the indirect indices, then the standard errors for those parameter estimates will likely be smaller.

Also, if you do find a package to do the complete analysis, the estimates of the parameters just using the direct indices would be good to have as starting values.  In any iterative algorithm, good starting values are your best friends.

Jim
